stances.label: Prohibit
stances.def: AI is not allowed.
stances.prose: The 9 prohibitions are stated by 119 universities, and 7 of them apply while students work. The most widespread forbids students to present AI-generated work as their own (P19.04), a rule stated by 94 universities in 132 statements. The others name particular dishonest uses, such as fabricating information or concealing AI use (P36.03, 16 universities), fabricating data, citations or evidence (P74.02, 12 universities) and forging records such as medical excuses (P74.15, 3 universities). One prohibition applies during assessment and treats unauthorized notes, devices or outside resources in an exam as cheating (P22.03, 9 universities), and no prohibition applies before the course, at its start, when misuse is suspected or over time.

parts.title: University, school and department policies
parts.intro: The institutional documents yield 266 policies that address instructors, merged from 5,590 statements at 303 universities. Policies cluster early in the course: 103 apply before it and 56 at its start, against 43 while students work, 12 during assessment and 10 over time; another 36 address suspected misuse and 6 give background facts. Over half of the policies, 152 of 266, take no position on AI and instead set duties, such as including an AI statement in the syllabus. Of the rest, 46 allow AI only for listed uses, 34 encourage it, 20 allow it with conditions, 8 leave the decision to the instructor, and 3 each prohibit AI or require something when it is used. Although only 8 policies leave the decision to the instructor, 252 of the 303 universities state at least one of them, and only the Duties and facts policies, at 282 universities, reach more.

parts.title: CS course policies
parts.intro: CS course syllabi say little about instructors. Across 19 universities, they yield 13 policies that address instructors, merged from 30 statements, compared with 266 policies from 5,590 statements in the institutional documents. The largest group, 5 of the 13, gives background facts, no other stage has more than 2 policies, and no course policy applies over time. By stance, 6 of the 13 take no position, 2 allow AI with conditions, 2 require something, and 1 each prohibits AI, allows it only for listed uses or encourages it; none leaves the decision to the instructor. Some are commitments the syllabus makes about the instructor's own conduct, such as never using AI to grade.
